3. For agent use, the ydotoold daemon should ideally be auto-started or the requirement clearly documented

Current behavior:
  tendril --display 1 run 'send("hello")'

title: DSL run requires --window to focus address bar; cmd+l reaches focused control instead of browser chrome
description: When driving Edge on macOS via tendril --window <id> run 'hold(cmd),send("l"),release(cmd)', the resulting Cmd+L is dispatched to whatever control already has keyboard focus inside the page (e.g. a search box on the current GitHub tab) rather than focusing the browser address bar. tendril correctly AXRaises the window/app, but Cmd+L arrives at the page-level focused element. AppleScript 'tell System Events to keystroke "l" using command down' (after a small delay) does focus the address bar reliably for Edge. Investigation: tendril's macOS keyboard injection path uses CGEventCreateKeyboardEvent via JXA; possibly missing a tiny pre-flight delay or not posting the event to the system-wide tap properly so the browser chrome receives the shortcut. Workaround today: shell out to osascript for browser-chrome shortcuts. Repro: open Edge with focused page input; tendril --window <edge-id> run 'hold(cmd),send("l"),release(cmd),send("about:blank"),Return' — text lands in the page input, not the URL bar.
creator: ms-mac:tendril:f6rtes1r9xdq86k0

title: Wayland input injection support (mouse/keyboard) for Hyprland and wlroots compositors
description:
Currently tendril run returns 'unsupported capability' on Wayland sessions. Input injection only works on X11 via xdotool/xte.

For Tendril to be useful for agent-driven browser/OS control on modern Linux desktops, Wayland input injection is critical. Most Linux desktops are Wayland-first now.

Possible approaches:
- wtype (wlroots-compatible keystroke injection)
- ydotool (kernel-level uinput, works across all sessions)
- Hyprland dispatch for window focus + virtual keyboard protocols
- wl-clipboard for text paste workflows

Current behavior:
  tendril --display 1 run 'hello'
  => error: unsupported capability: target does not support input execution

Expected: input injection works on Wayland, at least for Hyprland and wlroots compositors.
creator: helsinki:tendril:helsinki-tendril-tndl-ctrl

title: Make macOS Tendril binary self-contained; remove runtime Swift dependency
description:
Operator report: running Tendril on macOS currently fails during target discovery with `swift` missing at runtime (`error: tool 'swift' not found`). This violates the approved spec contract that every command is self-contained and causes an opaque platform adapter failure instead of reaching the expected permission-guided path (for example Screen Recording / Accessibility guidance).

Observed evidence:
- `crates/tendril/src/discovery.rs` shells out to `swift -e` for macOS target discovery.
- `crates/tendril/src/platform.rs` shells out to `swift -e` for multiple macOS input/focus paths.
- README/spec position Tendril as a self-contained binary and require structured permission/capability errors.

Required outcome:
- macOS `tendril list`, `capture`, and `run` must not require a runtime Swift toolchain/Xcode installation.
- The packaged binary must either use native Rust/linked platform APIs or another packaged self-contained mechanism.
- Missing macOS permissions must surface as structured permission guidance, not missing-tool/runtime adap failures.
- `nix run .#tendril` on macOS must be a supported operator path.
creator: ms-mac:tui

title: Wayland display/window capture fails: grim geometry format is wrong (WxH+X+Y instead of X,Y WxH)
description:
On a Hyprland Wayland session, tendril capture fails for both display and window targets with:

  platform adapter failure: Wayland capture failed via xdg-desktop-portal screenshot 
  ('Portal request didn't succeed: Other') and grim fallback ('grim failed: invalid geometry').

Root cause for grim fallback: The code in platform.rs capture_wayland_target_with_grim() builds geometry as:
  format!('{}x{}+{}+{}', width, height, x, y)  
  => e.g. '1920x1080+0+0'

But grim expects slurp-compatible format:
  'X,Y WxH'
  => e.g. '0,0 1920x1080'

Additionally, windows with negative coordinates (e.g. x=-1585 for off-screen windows) will produce invalid geometry strings for grim regardless of format.

The portal path also fails ('Portal request didn't succeed: Other') which may be a Hyprland xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland configuration issue, but the grim fallback should work when grim is installed.

Reproduction:
  tendril list --json  # shows display '1' at 0,0 1920x1080
  tendril --display 1 capture -o /tmp/test.png --json  # fails

Fix: Change geometry format string to '{x},{y} {width}x{height}' and handle negative coordinate windows gracefully.
creator: helsinki:tendril:helsinki-tendril-tndl-ctrl

title: Validate macOS Tendril parity with Linux Wayland — full command suite verification
description:
## Context
The Tendril controller on helsinki ran comprehensive hands-on validation on Linux/Wayland (Hyprland). macOS needs equivalent verification.

## Verified on Linux — macOS must match
- **list**: discovers displays+windows, correct IDs/bounds/scale, capabilities report input+capture=true
- **capture**: -o flag saves files, --max-width resize works, --json returns coordinate metadata, 10s timeout on unresponsive backends
- **run**: full DSL works — send(), lclick/rclick/mclick(x,y), hold/release(modifier), drag(), wait(), complex multi-action sequences, coordinate bounds checking
- **alias**: valid shell functions, rejects reserved words (if/for/while etc)
- **listen**: detects audio backend, probe_only for v0.0.1
- **mcp stdio**: Content-Length framed, initialize/tools/list/tools/call work, 3 tools exposed
- **error handling**: empty input, invalid DSL, missing target, out-of-bounds coords, invalid window ID, reserved alias — all return structured JSON errors
- **Nix packaging**: self-contained binary with all deps

## Critical agent workflow to verify end-to-end on macOS
list → capture screenshot → (interpret) → run input (click/type) → capture again
Test with a real GUI app: open browser, capture, click a link, capture result.

## macOS-specific concerns
- osascript/JXA for input — verify keystrokes and clicks actually arrive at target app
- screencapture for capture — verify actual images produced
- Accessibility permissions — verify structured permission errors when not granted
- CoreAudio detection for listen
- No Swift runtime dependency (fixed in bd-5c3937, re-verify)
- Coordinate mapping with Retina displays (2x scale factor)

## File beads for
- Any command working on Linux but failing on macOS
- macOS-specific unclear error messages
- Capability reporting differences
- Self-containment issues
- Retina coordinate mapping bugs
creator: helsinki:tendril:helsinki-tendril-tndl-ctrl

title: Verify Tendril controller runtime wake/self-nudge path in-session
description:
At controller startup on 2026-04-14, the Pi-managed persistent controller could not personally verify a real in-session wake/self-nudge or other runtime-native wake path. Per controller policy, autonomy must be treated as degraded until a real wake is observed.

Impact:
- The controller can perform manual health sweeps, but must not claim an autonomous monitoring/burndown loop is active.
- This weakens confidence that inbox/health checks will resume automatically after idle periods or daemon restarts.

Requested outcome:
- Verify that the Tendril project controller composition includes and actually triggers the intended Pi-native wake mechanism (for example pi-self-nudge / pi-loop as appropriate).
- If the wake path is absent or broken, fix the lifecycle/orchestration issue or document the supported wake mechanism and how controllers should verify it in-session.
- Confirm recovery with an observed in-session wake, not just configuration inspection.
creator: helsinki:tendril:helsinki-tendril-tndrl-ctrl

title: macOS key map missing 'delete' alias for backspace

Reproducer: tendril --window <id> run 'Delete'.

title: Linux audio backend detection fails when PIPEWIRE_RUNTIME_DIR and PULSE_SERVER env vars are unset despite active sessions
description:
Tendril's detect_linux_audio_backend() only checks three env vars:
- PIPEWIRE_RUNTIME_DIR
- PULSE_SERVER  
- PULSE_RUNTIME_PATH

On this system (NixOS, Hyprland, PipeWire+PulseAudio), none of these are set in the agent's environment, but both backends are fully operational:
- /run/user/1000/pipewire-0 socket exists
- /run/user/1000/pulse/native socket exists  
- pactl info works fine

Result: tendril listen fails with 'could not detect a supported audio backend' even though PipeWire and PulseAudio are both running.

Fix: Fall back to checking XDG_RUNTIME_DIR for pipewire-0 and pulse/native sockets when env vars are unset, or probe with pactl/pw-cli.
creator: helsinki:tendril:helsinki-tendril-tndl-ctrl

title: bug: tendril alias accepts shell reserved words as names, producing invalid shell code
description:
When a shell reserved word is used as the alias name, tendril generates shell code that fails with a syntax error when eval'd.

What I did:
  tendril --window w1 alias --name "if"

What I expected:
  Either a validation error rejecting the name, or a generated function that works.

What actually happened:
  Generates: if() { command tendril --window w1 "$@"; }
  This is a bash/zsh syntax error because 'if' is a reserved word.

All these fail: if, then, else, elif, fi, for, while, do, done, case, esac, function

The alias name validation already rejects spaces and special characters. It should also reject shell reserved words, at least for bash/zsh (the default shells).

Steps to reproduce:
  eval "$(tendril --window w1 alias --name if)"
  # => syntax error near unexpected token ')'
creator: ms-dev:tendril:ms-dev-tendril-test-user

title: Packaged Tendril on Hyprland still depends on host-side helper binaries instead of bundling/embedding them
description:
Hands-on test-user finding from bd-c82db3 on winmini (actual environment: NixOS + Hyprland/Wayland, not Windows).

What I did
1. Built the packaged Tendril binary: `nix build .#tendril`
2. Ran it successfully inside the live Hyprland session when the normal PATH was present.
3. Re-ran the packaged binary with a sanitized PATH containing only the Tendril binary directory, while preserving the live Wayland session env:

```bash
env -i HOME="$HOME" USER="$USER" LOGNAME="$LOGNAME" SHELL="$SHELL" \
  PATH="$(dirname "$PWD/result/bin/tendril")" \
  WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-1 DISPLAY=:0 \
  XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000 \
  DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus \
  HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE=59f9f2688ac508a0584d1462151195a6c4992f99_1776444819_1913698931 \
  "$PWD/result/bin/tendril" --json list
```

I also ran capture with the same sanitized PATH:

```bash
env -i HOME="$HOME" USER="$USER" LOGNAME="$LOGNAME" SHELL="$SHELL" \
  PATH="$(dirname "$PWD/result/bin/tendril")" \
  WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-1 DISPLAY=:0 \
  XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000 \
  DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus \
  HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE=59f9f2688ac508a0584d1462151195a6c4992f99_1776444819_1913698931 \
  "$PWD/result/bin/tendril" --json --display 1 capture
```

What I expected
- The packaged Tendril artifact to remain usable in a real Hyprland session without relying on separately installed host-side compositor/input helper binaries on PATH, or to ship/bundle the needed helpers with the release artifact.
- At minimum, packaged usability should not regress just because PATH is sanitized around the release binary.

What actually happened
- `list` failed with:
  `unsupported capability: Wayland discovery requires compositor metadata from one of the supported backends: Hyprland (hyprctl), sway (swaymsg), or wlroots output enumeration (wlr-randr); none detected on PATH.`
- `capture` failed with the same discovery error under the sanitized PATH.
- In the normal session PATH, `run` still reported no input support because `ydotool` and `wtype` were absent, so packaged Wayland input also still depends on external helpers for real usability.

Why this is a user-facing issue
- From an operator/test-user perspective, the packaged binary is not self-contained on Hyprland: discovery/capture depend on `hyprctl` being installed on the host PATH, and input depends on `ydotool`/`wtype` (plus `ydotoold` for the preferred backend).
- This makes the release artifact fragile and harder to use as a drop-in automation binary on real desktops.

Suggested direction
- Bundle the required helper tools with the packaged artifact, OR
- Replace the shell-outs with embedded/native integrations so the binary is self-contained on supported Wayland matrices.

Notes
- This appears related to the older closed self-containment work (`bd-d513d4`, `bd-e4edee`), but it is still reproducible in the current packaged artifact on a real Hyprland desktop.
creator: winmini:tendril:xikslu84b0dqi0sy

title: capture hangs indefinitely when portal and grim are unresponsive — needs timeouts
description:
On some Wayland sessions (Hyprland headless/sunshine), both the xdg-desktop-portal screenshot path and the grim fallback hang indefinitely. Tendril capture blocks forever with no timeout.

Reproduction:
  tendril --display 1 capture -o /tmp/test.png
  # hangs forever — must be killed

Root cause: Neither capture_wayland_target_via_portal() nor capture_wayland_target_with_grim() have timeouts. The portal D-Bus call blocks waiting for user interaction (or a broken portal), and grim blocks on compositor screenshot protocol.

Fix: Add configurable timeouts (e.g. 10s default) to both capture paths. On timeout, return a structured error like:
  { category: 'timeout', message: 'capture timed out after 10s — portal and grim both unresponsive' }

This is the most critical usability bug for agent use — an agent calling capture will hang its entire session.
creator: helsinki:tendril:helsinki-tendril-tndl-ctrl

title: Wayland portal capture spawns persistent xdg-desktop-portal-gtk dialog windows on each attempt
description:
Each failed tendril capture attempt on Wayland (Hyprland) spawns a new xdg-desktop-portal-gtk window that persists. After several capture attempts, tendril list shows 4+ portal dialog windows cluttering the target list:

  tendril list --json
  => 4 windows named 'xdg-desktop-portal-gtk' at 662,437 596x207

These appear to be authorization/confirmation dialogs that the portal spawns but never dismisses on failure. This pollutes target discovery and may confuse agents.

Either:
1. Suppress/dismiss the portal dialog automatically on failure, or
2. Filter known portal/system dialogs from target discovery, or  
3. Don't attempt portal capture when portal is known to not work (skip directly to grim), or
4. At minimum, document this as a known Wayland caveat

title: Wayland run without helper tools returns a generic target-level error instead of the documented actionable missing-backend diagnostic
description:
Hands-on test-user finding from bd-c82db3 on winmini (actual environment: NixOS + Hyprland/Wayland).

What I did
1. Ran Tendril in the live Hyprland session with the normal PATH.
2. Confirmed that no Wayland input helpers were installed:
   - command -v ydotool -> missing
   - command -v wtype -> missing
3. Ran documented run commands against discovered targets:
   - result/bin/tendril --json --window hypr:0x563e1e4d79d0 run 'send("hello")'
   - result/bin/tendril --json --display 1 run 'send("hello")'

What I expected
- An actionable Wayland missing-backend error that mentions both helper tools, matching the docs in docs/src/linux-wayland-operator-validation.md.
- The docs currently say that when no Wayland input backend is available, run should return unsupported_capability mentioning both ydotool and wtype and tell the operator to install at least one.

What actually happened
Both commands returned a generic target-scoped error instead:
- category: unsupported_capability
- code: input_not_supported_for_target
- message: unsupported capability: target does not support input execution

Example JSON error fields:
- status: error
- meta.command: run
- error.code: input_not_supported_for_target
- error.details.target_kind: display/window

Why this is a bug
- The error is much less actionable than the documented behavior. It hides the real remediation (install ydotool or wtype, and ydotoold for the preferred path).
- It contradicts the operator docs for the Wayland path.
- As a user, I cannot tell from the returned error whether the target is fundamentally unsupported or whether the host is just missing the expected helper backend.

Likely cause
- Discovery marks Wayland targets with input=false when no helpers are present, and run then fails early with a generic target capability check before surfacing the backend-specific missing-backend diagnostic.

Suggested fix
- On Wayland, if the session/backend is otherwise eligible but no helper backend is present, propagate the actionable missing-backend error from the Wayland input layer instead of the generic input_not_supported_for_target message, or update the docs if the current behavior is intentional.
creator: winmini:tendril:xikslu84b0dqi0sy

title: MCP stdio help advertises target flags that are accepted but ignored
description:
Hands-on test-user finding from bd-c82db3 on a live Hyprland/NixOS session.

What I did
1. Ran MCP help output:
   - result/bin/tendril mcp --help
   - result/bin/tendril mcp stdio --help
2. Noticed both help screens advertise target-scoping flags such as --window and --display (and also --json) on the MCP server launch command.
3. Verified that at least one of those flags is accepted but does not actually scope tool execution:
   - launched result/bin/tendril mcp stdio --window hypr:0x563e1e4d79d0
   - then sent an MCP tools/call request for capture with empty arguments {}
   - response was still a validation error saying capture requires exactly one of window or display

What I expected
- MCP server help to show only launch-relevant flags/options for the stdio server, or
- if launch-time target scoping is intentionally supported, MCP tool calls should actually inherit that scope.

What actually happened
- Help output advertises --window and --display on mcp / mcp stdio.
- Passing --window at server launch is silently ignored for tool execution.
- The first tool call still requires explicit window/display arguments in the MCP request body.

Why this is confusing
- The published MCP docs describe the launch contract as tendril mcp stdio and the target selectors as part of individual capture/run tool arguments.
- Seeing CLI target flags on the MCP server command implies they do something meaningful for the server process, but they do not.
- That makes the help text misleading for client authors and operators.

Suggested fix
- Hide irrelevant inherited global flags from mcp / mcp stdio help, or
- reject them explicitly on the MCP server path instead of accepting and ignoring them.

title: macOS: --window targeting activates app, not specific window (NSRunningApplication.activate)
description: On macOS, tendril --window <id> run ... calls NSRunningApplication.activate() which raises whichever window of that app is currently frontmost, not the requested window id. Found during bd-702f90 validation: send() into Ghostty window A landed in Ghostty window B. Workaround: prepend lclick(x,y) inside target bounds to raise the specific window. Fix ideas: AXUIElement / CGSOrderWindow to raise specific window by id, or document the click-to-focus prefix.
